Mammography Report 

Patient Name: Jane Doe
Date of Birth: July 10, 2000
Age: 25 years
Study Date: June 5, 2025
Referring Physician: Dr. Emily Carter, GP 
Procedure: Bilateral Mammography with Diagnostic Views 
Clinical Indication: Palpable lump in left breast, upper outer quadrant. Family history of breast cancer (mother, age 54). No prior imaging available. 

Technique:
Bilateral craniocaudal (CC) and mediolateral oblique (MLO) views were obtained. Additional spot compression and magnification views of the left breast were performed. 


Findings: 

Left Breast: 
A spiculated mass is seen in the upper outer quadrant of the left breast, approximately at the 10 o'clock position, 4 cm from the nipple. 
The lesion measures 2.8 cm in maximum diameter and shows irregular margins. 
Associated architectural distortion and surrounding parenchymal asymmetry are present. 
No skin thickening or nipple retraction identified on mammography. 
Clustered pleomorphic microcalcifications noted within the lesion. 

Right Breast:
Breast tissue is heterogeneously dense, which may obscure small masses. 
No suspicious mass, architectural distortion, or suspicious calcification is seen. 

Axillae:
Left axillary region shows enlarged lymph nodes, the largest measuring approximately 1.5 cm with cortical thickening (>3 mm).
Right axilla appears normal. 

---

Histopathology Report 

Patient Name: Jane Doe
Date of Birth: July 10, 2000
Age: 25 years
Study Date: Jul 6, 2025
Referring Physician: Dr. Emily Carter 
Specimen Submitted By: Dr. Lisa Hammond, Women’s Imaging Centre 
Date of Procedure: 07/06/2025 
Date of Report: 09/06/2025 
Specimen Type: Core biopsy – Left Breast Mass (10 o'clock position, 4 cm from nipple) 
Laboratory ID: PLD/25/0065378 


Macroscopic Description:
Five core biopsy specimens of soft tan-white tissue received in formalin, ranging from 1.2 to 1.8 cm in length. Entire tissue submitted for processing. 


Microscopic Description:
Sections show invasive epithelial malignancy composed of irregular nests, cords, and single malignant cells infiltrating fibrous stroma. 
Tumour cells exhibit moderate nuclear pleomorphism, prominent nucleoli, and moderate eosinophilic cytoplasm.
Frequent mitotic figures noted (>12/10 HPF).
Desmoplastic stromal response present.
Lymphovascular invasion not seen in the biopsy material.
No in situ component (e.g., DCIS) identified in the sampled cores. 


Immunohistochemistry (IHC) Results:

Marker		Result
----
Estrogen Receptor (ER)		Positive (90%)
Progesterone Receptor (PR)		Positive (80%)
HER2/neu Negative 		(Score 0)
Ki-67 Proliferation Index		35% 

 
 

Diagnosis: 
Left Breast Core Biopsy – Invasive Ductal Carcinoma, Grade II (Nottingham Score: 7/9) 
Hormone Receptor Status: ER Positive, PR Positive, HER2 Negative 
High proliferation index (Ki-67: 35%) 

 
 

Comment: 
The findings confirm invasive ductal carcinoma. Given the ER/PR positivity and HER2 negativity, the tumour is consistent with luminal B (HER2-negative) molecular subtype, which has implications for systemic therapy. Further clinical staging including axillary node status and imaging is recommended. Surgical excision and sentinel node biopsy should follow.
